findings.text: Traversal configuration holds one callback per table depth plus handlers for empty ranges and huge entries, predicates for pruning and per-region setup and teardown and an install hook, together with a selector describing what region locking the walker must take or assume.

Active walk state links the configuration, the target address space and its top table, the region currently visited, the directive chosen by the last callback, a flag permitting walks without a region, and an opaque caller cookie.

Single-address lookup result carries the resolved page, an indicator of the depth where it was found, a pointer to the table slot at that depth and a snapshot of that slot value, plus private region and table-lock state needed for release.

Walk locking offers four contracts: keep region structures steady under read access, acquire region write exclusion inside the traversal, or demand that the caller already holds region write or read exclusion with verification.

Callback directive distinguishes going deeper with large-page division when feasible, jumping past the entire child range to the following slot at the current depth, and repeating the callback for the identical slot.
Lookup depth is one of leaf, middle or upper huge-capable depths, and a single bitwise flag records whether the shared zero page is an acceptable result.

Walk synchronization requires the configured region-lock contract for the whole traversal, while a completed single-address lookup must release its table spinlock and, for leaf results, its temporary mapping and region walk guard.

Kernel table installation links a lower table into its parent slot inside the initial address space and, on platforms that flag the modified depth, requests synchronization of kernel mappings for the affected address.

Allocation tag identity is a compact integer handle, and a companion union represents a live reference either as a page pointer in compressed mode or as a pointer into page extension storage otherwise.
Tag identity space reserves zero for null, one for empty, and two as the first assignable value, with larger values partitioned between built-in and module ranges.

Conversion between integer identities and tag references treats null and empty specially and otherwise biases by the first assignable value to select built-in storage or delegate to module storage, with a fallback that warns and yields null identity on invalid input.

Tag reference lifetime supports two encodings, bitfield in page flags when compressed profiling is active and side storage otherwise, with paired acquire and release and an atomic flags update or direct pointer store respectively.

Tag query, clear, section init, split and swap helpers are inert when allocation profiling is disabled and otherwise forward to the accounting implementation, returning no tag when profiling is off or the reference is empty.
Middle and upper huge-page orders are defined as the difference between their respective table shifts and the base page shift.

Address-to-slot translation derives indices from the address and descends from the address-space root or the initial root through successive depths to middle and leaf slots, returning null for a virtual-to-leaf query when the middle slot is empty.

Leaf mapping has two platform variants, one creating a temporary local mapping of the page holding the leaf table and one using the directly addressable kernel window, both paired with an unmap that releases the RCU guard and any temporary mapping.

Lazy MMU batching maintains per-task nesting and pause counts, ignoring requests in interrupt context, entering hardware batch mode on the outermost enable, flushing on inner exit and leaving on the outermost exit, while pause temporarily exits and resume re-enters only when an outer batch is active; an alternate build provides inert operations.

Contiguous leaf operations advance address, slot pointer and frame number together, installing a run, clearing a run, or clearing while folding dirty and accessed state from the whole run into the returned value, with single-slot forms as the unit-count case.

Accessed and dirty handling provides test-and-clear at leaf and middle depths, selective clearing of either attribute over a run, capability queries for hardware tracking, and empty hooks for zapped-entry checks and TLB updates, with generic middle-depth defaults reporting absent.

Single-slot readers perform a one-shot volatile load at each depth, while split-word platforms reload the halves with ordering barriers until the low half is stable and pair the sequence with a table-reclamation synchronization that is empty on single-word platforms.

Destructive middle and upper huge-slot reads return the prior value after clearing the slot and notifying table checking, with full-teardown variants accepting but ignoring a full hint in the generic implementation, and leaf variants pairing clear with checking notification.

Miscellaneous table helpers expose middle-slot to page and folio conversion, empty initializers for leaf and middle tables, write-enable forwarding that ignores the region argument generically, and a leaf write-protect implemented as read-modify-write.
Generic access-flag installation and certain middle-depth young-state paths are declared unavailable and trap at build time rather than providing fallback behaviour.
Invalid module tag conversions and null page or reference handles trigger warnings and yield null results instead of proceeding, guarding against corrupt profiling metadata.

Walk-lock selectors are numbered zero through three in read, write, write-verify and read-verify order, walk directives zero through two in deepen, advance and repeat order, lookup depths ordered leaf then middle then upper, and the zero-page flag occupies bit zero.
Headers use include guards to prevent repeated inclusion within a single translation unit.
